optionNotes: Original lease: four 5-year options at $15.15 / $16.15 / $17.65 / $19.65/SF (on the 30,000 SF basis), exercisable on 6 months' notice, plus a 'January-31' fractional-period extension option (§13(b)). OfficeMax subsequently downsized to ~16,724 SF and is in possession on a short-term basis at $19.50/SF (1-year term 10/1/2025–9/30/2026 per the rent roll) — so the original $16.15/$17.65/$19.65 option track no longer governs. exclusives.description: OFFICE-SUPPLY exclusive (Lease, Prohibited Uses): no other Center space may be used for the sale of office/home-office/school/business products, computers and computer products, office supplies/equipment, office furniture, or office/home-office electronics (e.g. Office Depot, Staples, Workplace), or as a copy center / 'Kinko' operation. Carve-outs: incidental use ≤ the lesser of 2,000 SF or 10% of a user's floor (18% if the store is ≤2,000 SF), and ≤5,000 SF in the aggregate across the Center. (Whether this exclusive survives under the current short-term arrangement is unconfirmed — document not available.)

coTenancy.value: OfficeMax holds its OWN co-tenancy (Article 26, as replaced by the 1998 First Amendment): King Soopers OR one additional single-user retail tenant occupying >30,000 SF (the 'Major Tenants'), or permitted Replacement Tenants, must be open and operating at all times. If both Major Tenants AND the Replacement Tenants go dark (a 'Cotenancy Event'), OfficeMax may abate minimum rent and/or terminate. King Soopers is operating, so this co-tenancy is currently satisfied. (Likely modified/waived under the current short-term arrangement — unconfirmed.)

camTax.value: Real Estate Taxes (Art. 5): the Premises are not separately assessed, so Tenant pays a proportionate share of the Shopping Center's ad valorem taxes (excluding development/on-site special assessments). CAM (Art. 14): Tenant pays its proportionate share of common-area costs; Landlord maintains the roof, structure, exterior/demising walls, foundation and canopies. (Current short-term CAM/tax basis unconfirmed — document not available.)

flags.issue: Bearing on Michaels' co-tenancy — OfficeMax is a thin/temporary third anchor
flags.detail: OfficeMax is one of Michaels' three named co-tenancy anchors (King Soopers, OfficeMax, PetSmart). Because OfficeMax itself is a named 'Other Required Lessee', its short-term operation likely keeps Michaels at 3 of 3 FOR NOW — but the occupancy is short-term (ending ~9/30/2026 on the roll) and downsized (~16,724 SF, below the 21,000 SF / 70%-of-OfficeMax threshold that a REPLACEMENT tenant would need). When OfficeMax departs, Michaels falls to 2 of 3 (King Soopers + PetSmart) with no cushion. Worth tracking alongside the Michaels co-tenancy flag.

narrative: OfficeMax (OfficeMax North America, Inc., f/k/a OfficeMax, Inc.; store #0416 — now part of Office Depot/The ODP Corporation) occupies Unit 61 at University Hills, Denver under a 7/19/1996 lease for ~30,000 SF. The original deal was a 15-year term (~9/1/1997–8/31/2012) at $12.65 → $14.15/SF, with four 5-year options ($15.15 / $16.15 / $17.65 / $19.65/SF); OfficeMax exercised the first option (to 8/31/2017). The lease carries an office-supply exclusive and gives OfficeMax its own co-tenancy (King Soopers + one 30,000+ SF major tenant), while binding OfficeMax to the King Soopers, HomePlace and Just For Feet exclusives. OfficeMax has since left that option track and downsized: it is in possession on a SHORT-TERM basis of ~16,724 SF, which the April-2026 rent roll reflects as a one-year term (10/1/2025–9/30/2026) at $19.50/SF ($326,118/yr). The document that downsized the premises and set those short-term terms is not in the lease folder — flagged for Eric to provide. Practically, OfficeMax's short-term presence currently keeps Michaels' co-tenancy at 3 of 3, but it is temporary; on its departure Michaels drops to 2 of 3 with no cushion.
